title: From a bathroom scale to a weight forecast

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A smart scale measures far more than your weight. Body fat, muscle, water, even resistance in each limb. The catch is that all of it usually sits locked inside one phone app.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And Antoine wanted it next to everything else at home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. He wanted scale readings in Home Assistant, beside the rest of his apartment automations. So he forked hass_renpho, a community integration that pulls data from the Renpho cloud, and kept it going.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It logs into Renpho's cloud with the same account as the phone app and polls on an interval, six hundred seconds in his setup. Then it exposes sensors for weight, composition, metabolic estimates and device details. If a home connection gets blocked, there's an optional proxy setting.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How did he figure out the data fields?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: By reverse engineering. He ran a tool called APKLeaks over the Android app, which scans the package for hosts, paths and parameter names, a bit like reading the labels on every drawer in a cabinet. Then he matched those to the fields the integration already knew and filled the gaps.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what do you get at the end?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lovelace dashboards in Home Assistant: a weight history with composition gauges, and a second view for girth measurements and goals. Antoine opens it when training or sleep changes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Once the history was out of the app, he built a notebook with pandas and Keras. It starts with a linear trend line extended thirty days, then a random forest, then an LSTM neural network that reads a sliding window of past readings to predict the next one. A tuner searched unit counts and learning rates, and the best run used fifty-two units.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Any habits that make the data nicer?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three simple ones. Weigh at the same time of day, keep clothing constant, and watch trends over weeks instead of one morning. That's what keeps the curve meaningful. The full write-up has the dashboards, the sensor table and the notebook details.
